newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CREAM OF ETHIOPIAN SOCCER SEEKS ASYLUM IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CREAM OF ETHIOPIAN SOCCER SEEKS ASYLUM IN ITALY.

text.p: Sixteen members of Ethiopia's national soccer squad sought political asylum in Italy on Wednesday, leaving their country without a proper team after slipping their escort during a stopover on the way to a match.

The 15 players and their coach had been missing for more than 24 hours since disappearing from a hotel near Rome airport where they had been staying while on their way to Casablanca for an African Nations' Cup match against Morocco.

"We decided to ask for political asylum a long time ago but this was the first time we had an opportunity," one of the players, who gave his name as Yimam Mohammed, told reporters at Rome police headquarters.
Mohammed, acting as spokesman for the group, said an official team escort had always held on to players' passports during previous trips abroad.
"This time, though, we managed to get them from the reception of the hotel, where they may not have been told not to hand them over to the players," he said.

Seven members of the squad, which arrived in Italy on Monday afternoon from Addis Ababa, remained at the hotel. An Ethiopian soccer federation official in the capital, Sebsebe Haile Mariam, said they would fly home later on Wednesday.

The federation has already told the Cairo-based African Football Confederation that it would be unable to play Morocco. Mariam said it was meeting on Wednesday to decide whether to pull out of the African Nations' Cup altogether.

The missing 16 turned up at Rome police headquarters to register their asylum request with an Italian lawyer, Mario Lana. He said it was not clear whether they would be able to play soccer in Italy if their request was granted.
Mohammed said the group had checked out of the hotel in the early hours of Tuesday and spent the past night "on the streets" before going to a local office of the United Nations in Rome.
"We asked for the name of a lawyer and they put us in touch with Lana," he said.
"We want to stay here...I'm not going back to Ethiopia because of the political problems," another player said.
Lana said the 16 would be free to travel in Italy while awaiting an Italian decision on the asylum request.
Italian media said they could be looking for contracts with second or third division teams.
"It's too early to say if we can play in Italy. Now we are tired, very tired," Mohammed said.
It was not the first time that soccer players from Ethiopia, a former Italian colony, had asked for political asylum.

In 1991, 15 players in Egypt for the African Youth Soccer championship sought asylum. Six members of the Ethiopian soccer team asked to go to United States from Egypt in 1989 and in 1986 three players asked for political asylum in Swaziland.
